Biodiversity accross a fiber treatment

Roger Calvas

2025-04-10

Goals

Run an analysis on the within-sample biodiversity of the samples in our project.

  1. Calculate the Hill Numbers of the samples using the iNEXT package.
  2. Plot and evaluate the interpolated and extrapolated rarefaction curves from iNEXT.
  3. Analyze the Hill numbers as it relates to stations and salinity (in PSU).
  4. Test and then answer the scientific question at hand! (Remember, we’re doing biology!)

Inputs

  1. We will need the phytree_preprocessed_physeq, which includes a rooted tree (ideally within the archaea!) that we created in analysis/04B_Phylogenetic_Tree_Inspection.Rmd.

Outputs

This is an exciting analysis!!! We finally get to answer one of our scientific questions!

  1. Calculated biodiversity measures (Hill numbers) across every sample.
  2. Figures to include in our scientific paper that visualize the data as it relates to the scientific question.
  3. Statistical tests conveying the measured and quantified changes and patterns in biodiversity.

Scientific Question

Question & Hypotheses

How is produciton of short chain fatty acid modified in the gut microbiome after a dietary intervention with inulin?

  • Null Hypothesis: Concentrations of scf does not change after a treatment with inulin.
  • Alternative Hypothesis: Concentrations of scf in the gut increases after a treatment with inulin.

Set up the Environment

Timing of this script

# What time did we start running this script? 
start_time <- Sys.time()

Set the seed

set.seed(3980)

Load Packages & Colors

# install packages for stats
#install.packages("rstatix")
#install.packages("ggpubr")

pacman::p_load(tidyverse, devtools, patchwork, iNEXT, phyloseq,
               # packages for stats
               ggpubr, rstatix, install = FALSE)

# Load in colors for plotting 
source("code/colors.R")

  theme(legend.position = "none") + 
  labs(y = "Effective Number of ASVs", x = "Number of Sequences")

##   .. ..$ qD.LCL    : num [1:9177] 0.981 83.724 95.955 101.912 105.479 ...
##   .. ..$ qD.UCL    : num [1:9177] 1.02 87.12 99.7 105.88 109.58 ...
##  $ AsyEst  :'data.frame':    483 obs. of  7 variables:
##   ..$ Assemblage: chr [1:483] "SRR6443836" "SRR6443836" "SRR6443836" "SRR6443839" ...
##   ..$ Diversity : chr [1:483] "Species richness" "Shannon diversity" "Simpson diversity" "Species richness" ...
##   ..$ Observed  : num [1:483] 116 33.1 18.2 236 83.6 ...
##   ..$ Estimator : num [1:483] 116 33.2 18.2 236 84 ...
##   ..$ s.e.      : num [1:483] 1.987 0.293 0.216 2.033 0.591 ...
##   ..$ LCL       : num [1:483] 116 32.7 17.8 236 82.8 ...
##   ..$ UCL       : num [1:483] 119.9 33.8 18.7 240 85.1 ...
##  - attr(*, "class")= chr "iNEXT"
iNEXT_manual_df <- 
  iNEXT_data$iNextEst$size_based %>%
  dplyr::rename(names = Assemblage) %>%
  # join with the metadata
  left_join(., metadata_df, by = "names") %>%
  mutate(status = factor(status, levels = c("before",
                                              "during")))

# Inspection
dim(iNEXT_manual_df)
## [1] 19320    63
# Manually plot rarefaction curves 
iNEXT_manual_df %>%
  # Filter out rows that are calculated with actual sequences (no extrapolated)
  dplyr::filter(Method == "Rarefaction") %>%
  # Now, let's draw the plot! 
  ggplot(aes(x = m, y = qD, color = status, group = names)) + 
  geom_line() + 
  # Facet by station 
  facet_grid(Order.q~status, scales = "free") + 
  scale_color_manual(values = status_colors) + 
  theme_bw() + 
  labs(y = "Effective Number of ASVs", x = "Number of Sequences") + 
  theme(legend.position = "none")

#Interpretation 1: Sequencing depth is likely sufficient, all curves plateau even in richness. There is an outlier sample during the treatment that has an unusually high amount of ASVs, I will need to be in the lookout for that.

Run Shapiro-Wilk for the scf

# Test of the data is normal for the continuous value of butyrate
shapiro.test(metadata_df$Butyrate)
## 
##  Shapiro-Wilk normality test
## 
## data:  metadata_df$Butyrate
## W = 0.83628, p-value = 7.071e-12
# Test of the data is normal for the continuous value of acetate
shapiro.test(metadata_df$acetate)
## 
##  Shapiro-Wilk normality test
## 
## data:  metadata_df$acetate
## W = 0.83451, p-value = 3.588e-12
# Test of the data is normal for the continuous value of butyrate
shapiro.test(metadata_df$propionate)
## 
##  Shapiro-Wilk normality test
## 
## data:  metadata_df$propionate
## W = 0.6798, p-value = 2.706e-14
# Test of the data is normal for the continuous value of butyrate
shapiro.test(metadata_df$total_scfa)
## 
##  Shapiro-Wilk normality test
## 
## data:  metadata_df$total_scfa
## W = 0.85143, p-value = 4.009e-09

Now for the concentration of the 3 scf and total scfa, all of them had p-value<0.05 so none of them are normal, now we can look into richness

Now richness is not normal, so we need to use non parametric tests.

Kruskal wallis for the different scf

  obs_whole_rich_df %>%
